distribution.narrative: Lin & Beaver (2024) documents modern Taiwan material from Taichung City and Nantou County, including Ren’ai and Puli townships. Taiwan occurrence is confirmed; no mainland-China occurrence is established by this source. Beaver & Liu (2010) provides earlier accepted Taiwan occurrence evidence.

host_note: Direct Taiwan breeding records in Lin & Beaver (2024) support Machilus zuihoensis, Cinnamomum osmophloeum and Machilus thunbergii. The authors note a preference for Lauraceae and attacks on newly cut, dying or dead twigs/branches. Beaver & Liu (2010) gives only a broad statement that the species is polyphagous, with 10 species in 8 angiosperm families reported; that prose is retained at source level and does not expand the current host summary.
taxonomy_summary: The current accepted identity is Indocryphalus pubipennis (Blandford, 1894).
